entries.source: WHO IS THAT, HIDING OVER THERE?
SHE DETECTED HIM FROM THIS DISTANCE?!
entries.annotation_note: The wider photograph shows SHE and the whole balloon. The published Spanish changes him to us being here; the evaluation reference explicitly restores the English object.

entries.source: SHOULD I GIVE HER A BREAK AND SHOW MYSELF? I WANT TO ASK ABOUT DUNGEONS AND THAT "KI" SHE USED AFTER ALL...
entries.target: ¿Debería darle un respiro y mostrarme? Después de todo, quiero preguntarle sobre las mazmorras y ese "ki" que usó...
entries.annotation_note: Only the first complete photographed balloon is used, not the neighboring response. The causal after-all unit absent from the published Spanish is explicitly retained.
Only the first complete balloon is used; the neighboring panic dialogue is not merged. Hesitation filler is not a content criterion.

entries.source: N-NICE TO MEET YOU! I AM... ...NEW ADVENTURER!
entries.annotation_note: The two photographed parts of the same self-introduction (proposals 5 and 6) are combined; 6 is excluded as a duplicate. No article is invented in the English transcript.

entries.source: AND, BY MIXING UP BOTH OUR FORMS, I CAN MAKE AN ORIGINAL BODY, AND BE UNRECOGNIZABLE!
entries.target: Y al mezclar ambas formas, ¡puedo hacer un nuevo cuerpo que sea irreconocible!
entries.annotation_note: The visible sentence prefix in proposal 12 is joined to its completion in 11. Both Spanish parts are photographed; 12 is excluded as a duplicate.
Suspicious is ambiguous in isolated English. Do not automatically mark the other valid reading as a model content error without context.

entries.source: MY ADVENTURER RANK IS B, AND, UMM... AS YOU CAN SEE I AM A MARTIAL ARTIST.
entries.target: Mi rango de aventurera es B, y, umm... como puedes ver soy una artista marcial.
entries.annotation_note: The Spanish feminine is visible in the reference but is not inferable from this isolated English input. Gender alone is a needs-context case.

entries.source: SPRING HAS FINALLY COME FOR SOMEONE AS UNPOPULAR AS ME! I WILL DEFINITELY MAKE THIS HOT GUY MY BOYFRIEND!
entries.target: ¡Finalmente llegó la primavera para alguien tan impopular como yo! ¡Definitivamente haré a este chico atractivo mi novio!
entries.annotation_note: The published Spanish drops hot; the reference explicitly restores atractivo from the English pixels.

entries.source: MARTIAL ARTIST TAO JOINED YOUR PARTY!
entries.target: ¡La artista marcial Tao se ha unido a tu grupo!
entries.annotation_note: The reference is feminine from the artwork; a masculine article alone is unresolved by the isolated English input.

The whole English balloon is transcribed from the wider photograph. Aru is a character speech suffix, not an untranslated meaningful English word. Me in Spanish is contextual, not an explicit English object.

entries.source: DID YOU SEE THAT, ROBERTO! DID YOU FALL FOR ME-ARU?
I WAS PAYING ATTENTION, TAO. YOU'RE AMAZING!
entries.target: Te estaba prestando atención, Tao. ¡Eres increíble!

entries.source: WELL, YES. I COULDN'T FIND ANY DECENT MEN-ERR, ADVENTURER FRIENDS-ARU.
entries.target: Bueno, sí. No pude encontrar hombres... err, amigos aventureros decentes-aru.
entries.annotation_note: The published Spanish uses present puedo for past could not. The test reference explicitly restores past pude and makes the visible friends noun explicit; the male self-correction must not be silently discarded.
